# Control Narrative: Aggregate Conveying Line, Start/Stop and Protection

Module: CONV (VF-1, CV-1, CV-2, CR-1, CV-3). Requirement IDs use FR-CONV-NNN. Test methods: **S** = simulate input at FAT, **F** = functional run at FAT or SAT, **I** = inspection or wiring check.

## 1. Purpose and boundaries

This module starts, stops, and protects the line. Material flows from the hopper through VF-1, CV-1, CV-2, CR-1, and CV-3 to the stockpile.

- Upstream: hopper loading. This is outside the module.
- Downstream: stockpile. A plugged chute at the CV-3 discharge is the only stockpile interface signal.
- Pull-cord personnel protection is a safety function. It is specified in the safety requirements document (SRS-CONV, number to be assigned). This narrative only monitors its status.

## 2. Equipment and tags

Take instrument tag numbers from the instrument index. Do not copy them here.

| Equipment | Signals used by this narrative |
|---|---|
| CV-1, CV-2, CV-3 | Zero-speed switch, misalignment alarm switch, misalignment trip switch, pull-cords, plugged-chute switch, drive run feedback |
| CR-1 | Motor current transmitter (CT), lube oil pressure switch, drive run feedback |
| VF-1 | Drive run feedback |
| Line | Warning horn and beacon, HMI |

## 3. States and transitions (ISA-106)

| State | Entry permissive | Allowed exits | Initiator | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stopped | All drives off. No latched trip. | Starting | Operator (START on HMI) | Operator-initiated |
| Starting | Start permissives true (Section 6.1) | Running, Stopped (cancel), Aborting | Auto | Automatic |
| Running | All drives proven running | Stopping, Aborting | Auto | Automatic |
| Stopping | STOP, or HMI comms loss | Stopped, Aborting | Operator or auto | Automatic |
| Aborting | Any trip event | Aborted | Auto | Automatic |
| Aborted | All drives stopped. First-out trip latched. | Stopped | Operator (RESET on HMI) | Operator-prompted |

## 4. Regulatory control

None. The module has no control loops.

## 5. Sequences

### 5.1 Start sequence

The order is against the material flow. This prevents material from stacking on a stopped drive.

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Check start permissives. | All permissives true. | None | Reject START. Show unmet permissives. Stay Stopped. |
| 2 | Start horn and beacon. | Warning time elapsed. | SP-01 | Cancel or permissive loss: stop warning, go to Stopped. |
| 3 | Start CV-3. | ZSL of CV-3 shows motion. | SP-03 | Go to Aborting. |
| 4 | Start CR-1. | Lube pressure OK and current normal after the inrush time. | SP-22 | Go to Aborting. |
| 5 | Start CV-2 after the start delay. | ZSL of CV-2 shows motion. | SP-03 | Go to Aborting. |
| 6 | Start CV-1 after the start delay. | ZSL of CV-1 shows motion. | SP-03 | Go to Aborting. |
| 7 | Start VF-1 after the start delay. | VF-1 run feedback true. | SP-03 | Go to Aborting. |
| 8 | Stop horn and beacon. | None | None | None |

After step 8, the state is Running.

### 5.2 Normal stop sequence

The order follows the material flow. Each drive stops after its own run-out time. Each run-out time starts when the upstream drive stops.

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Stop VF-1. | VF-1 run feedback false. | SP-23 | Alarm. Continue. |
| 2 | Run out CV-1. Then stop CV-1. | Run-out time elapsed. | SP-05 | Alarm if ZSL of CV-1 shows motion after SP-23. Continue. |
| 3 | Run out CV-2. Then stop CV-2. | Run-out time elapsed. | SP-05 | Same as step 2. |
| 4 | Run out CR-1. Then stop CR-1. | Current at or below empty level for the confirm time. | SP-12 | Stop CR-1 at timeout. Raise "CR-1 stopped loaded" alarm. |
| 5 | Run out CV-3. Then stop CV-3. | Run-out time elapsed. | SP-05 | Same as step 2. |

After step 5, the state is Stopped.

## 6. Interlocks and permissives

The master logic is the cause-and-effect chart CE-CONV (number to be assigned). The tables below summarize intent only. If they differ from the chart, the chart governs.

### 6.1 Start permissives (all drives)

- No latched trip.
- All pull-cords healthy.
- No plugged-chute signal on any conveyor.
- No misalignment trip signal on any conveyor.
- Drive ready and in remote at the MCC.
- CR-1 lube oil pressure OK.
- Operator has confirmed CR-1 chamber clear after any CR-1 trip.

### 6.2 Protection response classes

| Class | Response |
|---|---|
| 1 | Stop all drives at once. |
| 2 | Stop the affected drive and all upstream drives at once. Downstream drives run out in flow order, then stop (as in 5.2). |
| 3 | Alarm only. |

### 6.3 Protection events

| Event | Class | Delay |
|---|---|---|
| Pull-cord operated on any conveyor | 1 | None (hardwired, see SRS-CONV) |
| Misalignment alarm stage | 3 | None |
| Misalignment trip stage | 2 on that conveyor | SP-15 |
| No motion at ZSL during start | Abort start; stop all started drives | SP-03 |
| Zero speed while running | 2 on that conveyor | SP-04 |
| Plugged chute at conveyor discharge | 2 on that conveyor | SP-16 |
| CR-1 current above high level | 3 | SP-09 |
| CR-1 current above high-high level | 2 on CR-1 | SP-09 |
| CR-1 lube pressure low while running | 2 on CR-1 | SP-14 (after SP-13 start bypass) |
| CR-1 current signal bad | 3, then 2 on CR-1 | SP-18 |

## 7. Alarms

Alarm priorities, set points, and responses are in the rationalized alarm database AL-CONV (number to be assigned, per ISA-18.2). This narrative does not restate them.

## 8. Abnormal handling

| Condition | Required behavior |
|---|---|
| Bad PV (CR-1 CT) | See Section 6.3. |
| Open circuit on any protection switch | Treat as the tripped state. |
| HMI comms loss longer than SP-17 | Run the normal stop sequence. |
| PLC power loss | All drives stop. They stay stopped on power return. |
| PLC restart | Go to Stopped. Do not restart any drive automatically. |
| Drive fail position | All drives stop on loss of command or power. |

## 9. Operator interface

- **Operator changes:** START, STOP, CANCEL (during warning only), RESET, and CR-1 chamber-clear confirmation.
- **Operator sees:**
  - line state and sequence step
  - per-drive run and fault status
  - unmet start permissives
  - first-out trip
  - run-out countdown
  - CR-1 current trend
- **Operator prompts:** "Confirm CR-1 chamber clear" and "Reset trip".

## 10. Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-CONV-001 | The line must start only from the control room HMI. | F |
| FR-CONV-002 | The PLC must reject START if a start permissive is false. | S |
| FR-CONV-003 | The PLC must show each unmet permissive on the HMI. | S |
| FR-CONV-004 | On accepted START, the PLC must start the horn and beacon. | F |
| FR-CONV-005 | No conveyor may move until the warning time (SP-01) has elapsed. | F |
| FR-CONV-006 | CANCEL during warning must stop the warning and return to Stopped. | F |
| FR-CONV-007 | Loss of a permissive during warning must stop the warning and return to Stopped. | S |
| FR-CONV-008 | The start order must be CV-3, CR-1, CV-2, CV-1, VF-1. | F |
| FR-CONV-009 | The PLC must start each drive only after the previous drive is proven, plus SP-02. | F |
| FR-CONV-010 | A conveyor is proven when its ZSL shows motion within SP-03. | S |
| FR-CONV-011 | CR-1 is proven when lube pressure is OK and current is normal after SP-10. | S |
| FR-CONV-012 | A proof failure in the start sequence must stop all started drives. | S |
| FR-CONV-013 | The horn and beacon must stop when VF-1 is proven. | F |
| FR-CONV-020 | The stop order must be VF-1, CV-1, CV-2, CR-1, CV-3. | F |
| FR-CONV-021 | Each conveyor must run out for its own time in SP-05 before it stops. | F |
| FR-CONV-022 | CR-1 must stop when current is at or below SP-11 for SP-24, or at SP-12. | S |
| FR-CONV-030 | A pull-cord must stop all drives through the hardwired safety circuit. | F, I |
| FR-CONV-031 | The PLC must not be in the pull-cord stop path. | I |
| FR-CONV-032 | A misalignment alarm stage must raise an alarm only. | S |
| FR-CONV-033 | A misalignment trip stage must give a Class 2 response after SP-15. | S |
| FR-CONV-034 | Zero speed on a running conveyor for SP-04 must give a Class 2 response. | S |
| FR-CONV-035 | A plugged chute for SP-16 must give a Class 2 response. | S |
| FR-CONV-036 | CR-1 current above the high-high level for SP-09 must give a Class 2 response. | S |
| FR-CONV-037 | The PLC must ignore CR-1 current high-high during the SP-10 inrush time. | S |
| FR-CONV-038 | Low lube pressure for SP-14 after SP-13 must give a Class 2 response on CR-1. | S |
| FR-CONV-039 | A bad CR-1 CT signal for SP-18 must give a Class 2 response on CR-1. | S |
| FR-CONV-040 | Downstream drives must run out and stop in flow order after a Class 2 trip. | F |
| FR-CONV-041 | All trips must latch. | S |
| FR-CONV-042 | RESET must work only when the cause is clear. | S |
| FR-CONV-043 | After a CR-1 trip, the operator must confirm chamber clear before the next start. | F |
| FR-CONV-044 | A restart after any trip must use the full start sequence, including the warning. | F |
| FR-CONV-045 | The PLC must treat an open circuit on any protection switch as tripped. | I, S |
| FR-CONV-046 | HMI comms loss longer than SP-17 must start the normal stop sequence. | S |
| FR-CONV-047 | After power loss or PLC restart, no drive may start without an operator START. | F |

- Each requirement has an ID and a test method.
